title.rendered: How to Get Clients in Construction: 10 Proven Strategies

content.rendered:
Are you looking to grow your construction business but struggling to fill your project’s pipeline? In today’s competitive industry, knowing how to get clients in construction is crucial for success. Whether you’re a seasoned professional or just starting out, implementing effective strategies to attract and retain clients can make all the difference in your business growth and sustainability.

This article will explore ten proven strategies to help you secure more clients in the construction sector. From leveraging your network and optimising your online presence to providing exceptional service and utilising email marketing, we’ll cover a range of tactics that can boost your lead generation efforts. You’ll discover how to take advantage of social media, gather compelling testimonials, and make the most of trade shows to showcase your expertise and win more projects.

How to Get Clients in Construction: Leverage Your Network and Referrals

In the construction industry, your network is a goldmine for securing new clients. To get clients in construction, start by tapping into your existing connexions. Reach out to past clients, colleagues, and industry partners. These relationships can lead to valuable referrals and new opportunities.

Networking events are a fantastic way to expand your connexions. Attend industry-specific gatherings, such as the Women in Construction Networking Event at London Build Expo. These events allow you to meet influential figures in the UK construction industry and exchange business cards.

Don’t underestimate the power of testimonials. They highlight your competitive advantages and build trust with potential clients. To get quality testimonials, provide clients with a questionnaire soon after project completion. Ask open-ended questions that prompt descriptive responses about your strengths. Keep testimonials concise, focusing on your company’s unique selling points.

Remember, partnering with other professionals can also lead to new clients. Collaborate with architects, suppliers, or complementary trades to expand your reach and tap into their client base.

Optimise Your Online Presence: A Key Strategy for How to Get Clients in Construction

Another proven strategy on how to get clients in construction, you need a strong online presence. Start by creating a user-friendly website that showcases your projects and services. Make sure it’s mobile-responsive, as many potential clients browse on smartphones. Implement SEO strategies to improve your visibility in search results. Use relevant keywords throughout your site and create quality content that addresses common questions in the construction industry.

Don’t forget the power of social media. Platforms like Instagram and Facebook are ideal for sharing visuals of your completed projects. LinkedIn can help you connect with industry professionals and potential clients. Regularly post updates, behind-the-scenes content, and employee spotlights to humanise your brand.

Consider setting up a Google My Business profile to appear in local search results. Encourage satisfied clients to leave reviews, as these can significantly boost your credibility. Remember, your online presence is often the first impression potential clients have of your business, so make it count.

Content Marketing for Construction: Attract Clients with Valuable Content

Creating high-quality content is an effective way to attract and engage potential clients and is a key component of how to get clients in construction. By providing valuable information and establishing your expertise, you can position your business as a trusted resource and generate leads.

Here are some content marketing ideas for construction:

  • Blog posts: Share informative articles on topics relevant to your target audience, such as “How to Choose the Right Contractor for Your Project” or “Tips for Renovating Your Home on a Budget.”
  • Case studies: Showcase your successful projects by creating detailed case studies that highlight your skills and capabilities.
  • White papers and ebooks: Offer in-depth reports or guides on specific construction topics to demonstrate your expertise and provide value to potential clients.
  • Videos: Create engaging videos that showcase your projects, introduce your team, or provide educational content related to construction.

When you consistently create and share valuable content, you can attract potential clients, build brand awareness, and establish your business as a leader in the construction industry.

Provide Exceptional Service and Follow-Up: Essential for How to Get Clients in Construction

To get clients in construction, you need to deliver outstanding service and maintain strong relationships. Start by clearly defining expectations for all project stakeholders. Communicate quickly and effectively to prevent delays and keep everyone on the same page. Use project management software to document hours, materials, and other crucial information.

Listen actively to your team’s perspectives and foster good working relationships. Embrace digital solutions like cloud-based construction management software to streamline communication and collaboration. This ensures real-time updates and centralised information access for all involved parties.

Remember, effective communication is the cornerstone of success in construction. Establish clear channels for information flow to avoid misunderstandings that can lead to costly mistakes. By prioritising exceptional service and follow-up, you’ll build a reputation for reliability and quality, attracting more clients to your construction business.

How to Get Clients in Construction Through Email Marketing

Email marketing can be a powerful tool for how to get clients in construction. By building an email list of potential clients and industry contacts, you can nurture relationships, promote your services, and generate leads.

Here are some email marketing tips for construction:

  • Offer valuable content: Provide subscribers with informative content, such as industry news, project updates, or tips for homeowners.
  • Showcase your projects: Highlight your recent work and successful projects to demonstrate your expertise and capabilities.
  • Promote special offers: Offer exclusive discounts or promotions to email subscribers to encourage them to contact you.
  • Personalise your emails: Address subscribers by name and segment your list to send targeted messages based on their interests and needs.

By using email marketing strategically, you can stay top-of-mind with potential clients and nurture them through the sales funnel.

How to Get Clients in Construction – Final Verdict

Securing clients in the construction industry requires a multifaceted approach. By harnessing the power of your network, optimising your online presence, and delivering exceptional service, you can set your business apart from the competition. These strategies, combined with effective communication and a strong digital footprint, have a significant impact on your ability to attract and retain clients in this competitive field.

Remember, success in construction is not just about winning projects, but also about building lasting relationships. By consistently applying these proven tactics, you’ll be well-positioned to grow your business and establish a solid reputation in the industry. title.rendered: How to Organise a Construction Site: A Practical Setup Guide

content.rendered:
Knowing how to organise a construction site properly is the difference between a project that runs to programme and one that bleeds time, money and goodwill. A disorganised site costs you through double-handling, near misses, rework, and a workforce that spends half the day searching for materials or waiting on late deliveries. If you are running a construction business at £1M or above, site-level inefficiency quietly kills your margins. This guide gives you a practical framework covering everything from day one on site through to handover: planning, layout, compliance, deliveries, safety, quality and waste.

Plan the Site Before Work Starts

Before a machine rolls on site, you need a site organisation plan. That means walking the plot, understanding the access constraints, and mapping out where everything will go before a single trade books in.

Start with a pre-construction survey. Note the ground conditions, any underground services (check with Dial Before You Dig), overhead lines, existing structures and neighbouring properties. On a £500k residential scheme this takes a morning. On a £3M commercial project it can take several days and involve structural engineers and services specialists.

From the survey, establish:

  • The principal access point for deliveries and personnel
  • Where the site compound will sit, including welfare cabins, skip positions and secure storage
  • Laydown areas for materials, zoned by trade and programme phase
  • Crane or plant positions, with turning circles and load-bearing capacity confirmed
  • Temporary services connections: water, power and drainage

The CDM Regulations 2015 require a Principal Contractor to produce a Construction Phase Plan before work starts. This is not a tick-box exercise. It should describe how the site will be managed, what the significant risks are, and how you will control them. If you are the PC on the project, this document is one of your most important legal duties and it shapes everything else.

Get the programme locked in at this stage too. A Gantt chart showing key milestones, trade sequence and material lead times will drive every decision you make on site. If you’re running several projects simultaneously, a shared project management platform keeps your managers aligned without you needing to be present everywhere. Our guide to successful construction project management goes deeper on planning and running multiple contracts at once.

Design the Site Compound and Layout

A well-designed site compound doesn’t happen by accident. Get this wrong and you pay for it every single day of the project.

The compound is the hub: welfare facilities, the site office, tool storage, PPE dispensing and materials laydown. Locate it close to the main entrance so deliveries can be checked in and directed without vehicles crossing the working area. That one decision can save hours of disruption every week.

Welfare facilities are a legal requirement under CDM 2015 and the Construction (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations. On any active site you must provide:

  • Toilets, at minimum one per 25 workers on larger sites
  • Washing facilities with hot and cold running water
  • A rest area with seating, tables and a means of boiling water
  • Facilities for changing and drying clothes, with lockers for personal belongings

On a 20-person site, budget around £600 to £900 per month for welfare cabin hire. That is a small fraction of your weekly wage bill, and it has a direct effect on morale and productivity. Workers who have somewhere decent to eat and dry off work harder and stay longer.

Mark out pedestrian and vehicle routes separately. This sounds obvious but it is one of the most commonly missed causes of near misses on smaller sites. Heras fencing and clear signage cost almost nothing relative to the cost of an HSE prohibition notice or a reportable incident.

Zone your materials storage by trade and by programme phase. Bricklayers’ materials should not occupy the space where your groundworkers need to operate in week two. Plan this on paper before anything arrives on site and brief every subcontractor on the layout before they start.

Documentation and CDM Compliance

A site that is well-organised on paper is far easier to run on the ground. Good documentation protects you legally, keeps your team working clearly, and gives clients and main contractors confidence they are dealing with a professional operation.

The documents that must be active and accessible on site at all times:

  • Construction Phase Plan, updated as the project evolves
  • Health and Safety Policy
  • Risk Assessments and Method Statements (RAMS) for every significant activity
  • Permits to Work for high-risk tasks: hot works, confined spaces, excavations and working at height
  • F10 Notification if the project is notifiable under CDM
  • Competency records, CSCS cards and trade certificates for everyone on site
  • Insurance certificates
  • COSHH assessments for any hazardous substances in use

Set up a site document folder, physical in the site office or digital using a platform like Procore, Buildertrend or a well-structured shared drive. The test is simple: if the HSE walked on site today, could you put your hands on every relevant document within five minutes? If not, sort it before they show up.

Permits to Work deserve particular attention. A hot works permit should require a formal sign-off before work starts and a fire watch of at least 30 to 60 minutes after work ends. A signed RAMS record also protects you commercially. If a subcontractor later claims they were not briefed on a specific risk, your documentation answers that straight away.

Building repeatable, standardised systems for site documentation is one of the hallmarks of a construction business that scales reliably. For more on this, see our guide to effective construction business systems that work across multiple projects without depending on you personally.

Manage Deliveries and Materials

Uncontrolled deliveries are one of the most common causes of site chaos. A delivery management system is central to how you organise a construction site day to day. Lorries turning up unannounced, blocking access, depositing materials in the wrong place or arriving when nobody is available to unload them can cost hours you will never recover.

Build a delivery management process in from the start:

  • Issue a delivery schedule to all suppliers at project start, with confirmed time slots by trade
  • Designate a site manager or banksman responsible for accepting deliveries and directing vehicles
  • Check every delivery note against the purchase order and count or measure the load before signing
  • Assign a clearly marked laydown area for each trade and decline deliveries that cannot be correctly stored

On a £2M project you could be co-ordinating concrete pours, scaffold erections, steelwork drops and plant movements on the same day. A shared weekly delivery matrix, circulated to all subcontractors at the Monday morning briefing, is not over-engineering. It is basic site control.

Materials theft costs the UK construction industry an estimated £800 million per year. Secure your compound with Heras fencing, padlocked storage containers, CCTV and decent lighting. Keep the most valuable materials, copper pipework, power tools, premium timber, inside locked containers overnight. A monitored CCTV system on a 12-month project typically runs to £1,500 to £3,000 in hire costs. A single significant theft almost always costs more than that.

Double-handling is the silent killer of site margins. If a material gets offloaded in the wrong place and moved three times before it reaches the point of use, you are effectively paying for that labour four times over. Plan the laydown and it pays for itself within weeks.

Safety, Welfare and Daily Site Briefings

Site safety is not just PPE and signage. It is about how the site runs day to day: who is briefed, who is accountable, and what the response is when something goes wrong.

Start each morning with a five-minute site briefing. Cover the plan for the day, any specific risks from that day’s activities (a crane lift, a concrete pour, hot works), and any changes to access or working areas. Five minutes at the start prevents days of lost time, or worse.

Every person must complete a site induction before entering the working area, including subcontractor directors and client representatives. At minimum, cover:

  • Site rules and emergency procedures
  • Location of the first aid kit and named first aiders
  • Fire assembly point
  • Reporting procedures for accidents and near misses
  • Site-specific hazards and any restricted zones

PPE requirements should be displayed at the site entrance and enforced without exception. Hard hats, hi-vis and safety footwear are the baseline. Specific activities require more: RPE for dust exposure, face shields for grinding, harnesses for work at height.

Track who is on site at all times. A signing-in sheet, or a digital access system on larger projects, gives you an accurate headcount for emergency evacuation and a record for payroll verification. Beyond the rules, a safe site culture comes from how you and your managers behave every single day. Getting a team to run safely without you policing every move requires genuine delegation. The principles in our guide to delegation in construction apply directly here.

Quality Control from Day One, Not Just Before Handover

Knowing how to organise a construction site well includes building quality checks into the daily workflow, not adding them on at the end when the damage is already done and the snagging list runs to three pages.

For each trade package, create a simple inspection checklist tied to the programme:

  • Brickwork: check for plumb, coursing and joint consistency before the scaffold is struck
  • First fix electrics and plumbing: sign off before linings go on
  • Structural elements: inspect against drawings before pours or cover-up
  • Drainage: test and record before backfill

Run a snag management process throughout the project, not just in the final two weeks. Assign each snag to the trade responsible and track resolution against a deadline. On a project worth £1M or more, unresolved snagging at handover can hold up tens of thousands of pounds in retention and delay your final payment by months.

Stage-gate inspections at key milestones, foundations complete, structure up, watertight, first fix done, second fix done, give your client visible reassurance and give you early warning before problems compound. The quality of your handover is what clients remember when they are deciding whether to refer you or call you for the next job.

Environmental Responsibility and Waste Management

Environmental responsibility is a legal requirement, not an optional extra. A Site Waste Management Plan (SWMP) is good practice on any project above £300,000 in value and a legal requirement in Scotland.

Plan for waste from the outset:

  • Identify the waste streams your project will generate: concrete, timber, plastics, excavated material
  • Position skips and segregation bays close to the point of arisings, not just wherever is convenient for the first delivery
  • Brief every trade on segregation requirements before they start work
  • Keep waste transfer notes for every load leaving site, both for compliance and cost tracking

Controlling dust, noise and water runoff keeps you on the right side of the Environment Agency and prevents neighbour complaints that escalate into enforcement action. Wheel wash facilities on any site with significant vehicle movements stop concrete and mud tracking onto public highways, which carries its own liability and clean-up cost.

A clean, well-maintained site also sends a clear signal to clients, passing trade and anyone considering working with you. It costs nothing extra and it is free marketing every day the project runs.

Build a Site Setup System That Scales with Your Business

The difference between a construction business running at £1M and one running at £3M or £5M is not simply more jobs. It is the ability to run multiple well-organised sites simultaneously without the owner needing to be present on every one.

That requires your site setup process to become a documented system: a repeatable checklist and briefing pack that a site manager can execute without you holding their hand. Every element covered in this guide, from compound layout and document folders to morning briefings and stage-gate inspections, should be written down and standardised so that quality of execution does not depend on which manager is in charge that week.

When the way you organise a construction site is consistent across every project, your margins become more predictable, your team grows in confidence, and your reputation builds. Clients and main contractors notice the difference between a controlled site and a chaotic one. It affects which contracts you get offered and the price you can hold.

Two guides worth reading alongside this one: the seven mistakes most construction businesses make when scaling past £1M, and our practical walkthrough of how to scale your construction business past the growth plateaus that catch most owners out.

Ready to Build a Better-Run Business?

Getting your sites running cleanly is one part of moving from £1M toward £3M or £5M in turnover. The businesses that make that jump successfully build proper systems around every part of their operation: site delivery, financial control, pricing, marketing and team management.

At Develop Coaching we work with UK construction business owners to put those systems in place and remove the bottlenecks that stop growth. If you want to find out how we can help your business grow without it consuming you, speak to our construction business coaching team for a no-obligation conversation about where you want to get to and what is standing in the way.

title.rendered: Setting Clear Construction Business Goals for 2025

content.rendered:
As you set your sights on 2025, it’s time to think big for your construction business. Setting clear goals is not just about boosting profits; it’s about shaping a vision that drives your company forward. Whether you’re looking to improve project management, boost productivity, or gain a competitive advantage, having well-defined construction business goals is key to your success.

In this article, we’ll explore how to craft a robust mission statement and strategic plan for your construction firm. You’ll discover ways to enhance time management, assess risks more effectively, and improve financial management. We’ll also delve into methods for fostering business growth, increasing profitability, and embracing the latest industry trends. Get ready to build a strong foundation for your company’s future!

Define Your Construction Business Goals: Start with a Vision

To set clear construction business goals, you need to start by defining your company’s vision. This involves crafting a mission statement that captures the heart of your business. Here’s how to do it:

  1. Describe your core services and ideal clients in a few sentences
  2. Highlight what makes your company special
  3. Think about your biggest challenges and turn them into goals
  4. Review and update your brand if needed
  5. Identify your core values and mission

Remember, your mission statement should be concise, easy to understand, and memorable. It should guide your decision-making and inspire your team. By clearly defining your vision, you’ll have a strong foundation to build your goals.

Setting SMART Construction Business Goals

While having a clear vision is essential, it’s equally important to set SMART construction business goals. SMART stands for:

  • Specific: Clearly define what you want to achieve. Avoid vague goals like “increase profits.” Instead, set a specific target, such as “increase profits by 15% in the next year.”
  • Measurable: Establish metrics to track your progress and measure your success. This could involve tracking key performance indicators (KPIs) like profit margins, project completion rates, or client satisfaction scores.
  • Achievable: Set realistic goals that are challenging yet attainable. Avoid setting goals that are too ambitious, as this can lead to discouragement and demotivation.
  • Relevant: Ensure your goals align with your overall business vision and strategic direction. Each goal should contribute to the bigger picture of where you want your company to be.
  • Time-bound: Set deadlines for achieving your goals. This creates a sense of urgency and helps you stay focused and on track.

By following the SMART framework, you can set construction business goals that are clear, actionable, and more likely to be achieved.

Prioritise Sustainable Growth to Achieve Your Construction Business Goals

To set your construction business up for success in 2024, you need to focus on sustainable growth. Here’s how you can achieve this:

Expand into new markets

Reach a wider audience and bring in more work. This can help you weather economic turbulence by diversifying your revenue streams.

Offer new services

Grow organically by expanding into areas adjacent to your current business. For example, if you build roads, consider branching out into bridge construction.

Consider mergers and acquisitions

This can be a quick way to gain new skills and clients. Look for businesses with similar values and culture.

Embrace sustainability

Incorporate eco-friendly practises and materials. This can attract environmentally conscious clients and open up new market opportunities.

Invest in your team

Provide training and development to ensure your workforce can deliver new services effectively.

By prioritising sustainable growth, you’ll be better positioned to thrive in the ever-changing construction landscape and achieve your construction business goals.

Focus on Client Satisfaction

To set clear construction business goals, you need to prioritise client satisfaction. Happy clients are more likely to lead to repeat business and positive referrals, which contribute to your overall construction business goals. Here’s how you can achieve this:

  1. Improve communication: Keep clients informed with regular updates and thorough status reports. Use dashboards to provide real-time project information and key metrics.
  2. Engage clients actively: Involve them in lessons-learned sessions throughout the project lifecycle. This shows you value their input and are committed to continuous improvement.
  3. Demonstrate commitment: Have a C-level representative participate in project meetings or visit the site. This sends a powerful message that the client is a priority.
  4. Streamline processes: Focus on smooth project closures and efficient user acceptance testing. These often-overlooked areas can significantly impact client experience.

By focusing on these aspects, you’ll not only meet but exceed client expectations, fostering strong, lasting relationships and driving your business forward.

Embrace Digital Transformation

To stay ahead in the construction industry, you need to embrace digital transformation. Here’s how:

  • Adopt Building Information Modelling (BIM) for better collaboration and efficiency
  • Implement prefabrication techniques to reduce waste and improve quality control
  • Use drones for surveying, mapping, and monitoring project progress
  • Explore 3D printing for creating complex architectural designs
  • Leverage IoT devices to gather real-time data and spot safety concerns
  • Consider blockchain for improved data transparency and collaboration
  • Integrate AR and VR technologies for visualising designs and training workers

By embracing these technologies, you’ll boost productivity, enhance safety, and gain a competitive edge in the ever-evolving construction landscape.

Successfully Setting Clear Construction Business Goals

Setting clear goals for your construction business has a significant impact on shaping your company’s future. By focusing on defining your vision, prioritising sustainable growth, enhancing client satisfaction, and embracing digital transformation, you’re laying a strong foundation for success. These strategies provide a roadmap to navigate the challenges and opportunities in the ever-changing construction landscape.

As you move forward, remember that goal-setting is an ongoing process. Regularly review and adjust your objectives to stay aligned with industry trends and your company’s evolving needs. By staying committed to your vision and adapting to new technologies and practises, your construction business is well-positioned to thrive in 2025 and beyond. Keep building on your strengths, addressing weaknesses, and seizing opportunities to construct a prosperous future for your company.

title.rendered: Top tips to become financially free

content.rendered:
As a fellow business owner, I know that we all have the goal of having more freedom and also making more money for our company. This is why we work hard to try to scale up and grow. I recently chatted to entrepreneur Jason Greystone, who gave me some great tips on what it takes to become financially free as a business owner.  

 

Jason was able to become financially free before the age of 30, which meant having an income generated by systems that didn’t rely on him to work. He started in the construction industry, and through his business savvy and experience got to where he is today.  

 

I really wanted to get his feedback on how he developed this freedom. When we spoke he told me that financial freedom isn’t about working harder and having a higher net-worth, but it is created from having a free mind.  

 

Jason gave me three tips that he found useful in his journey to free his mind and ensure financial freedom. They were: 

 

  1. 1. Manage your time wisely.

  3. Think about what actions you can take that will give you back time. One thing that works really well for this is time blocking, setting aside specific time in your schedule for tasks and making sure you stick to it. Also ask yourself: What systems can I use to replace my work to give me more time? Look at your business closely and put these systems in place as soon as you can to start getting the benefits.  

  5. 2. Make sure you delegate.

  7. All of the jobs you don’t like and find a struggle, delegate it to someone else. Ask yourself: How much of your income do you need to be able to delegate these tasks elsewhere? Doing this will mean that you have the time and headspace to work on developing your business.  

  1. 3. Try to be mobile.

  3. Being mobile is 70% of being free. All you have to do after that is work out how to make your income more passive, and then you can achieve total financial freedom.  

 

Jason also said that having six months of living costs in cash, in the bank, can be another way to free your mind. It will take the pressure off and also help you to enjoy your work more. It will change your outlook and make you more free to explore opportunities in your business.   

 

To hear more of Jason’s advice, make sure you check out Episode 4 of the Develop your construction business Podcast here.

title.rendered: What we can learn from Mount Everest

content.rendered:
At just over 29,000 ft, Mount Everest is a formidable mountain to conquer. It is on the list of many mountaineers and thrill-seekers as one to tick off, but if anyone attempted to climb unprepared they would be in danger of losing their lives. Anyone who wants to climb and be successful needs a plan. And in a lot of ways as business owners, we are in the same position, it’s not enough to have a goal to earn a certain amount of money or to grow your business, you need a plan to get there.  

 

So at the start of a new year, I thought it would be helpful to take a look at the successful climbers of Everest and see what we can learn from them. 2022 is the year when you as a business owner can climb your Everest.  

 

Take it in stages  

 

Climbing Everest isn’t possible in one go, you need to take it in stages to be safe. There are six stages you need to take on to get to the top, each with its challenges.  

The first stage is to get to the base camp, which will lay the foundation that will help you climb up the rest of the steps. Then Camp 1 sits at 20,000 ft, and the route to get there is over a moving glacier. Camp 2 is a bit flatter but can go from extremes in temperature which can be mentally tougher than the steep climbs. When you get to the 2nd camp you can see the peak of Everest for the first time. Camp 3 is difficult as there is an ice wall that needs to be traversed. The camp itself is like an eagle’s nest, perched on the edge of the mountain, and is dangerous. But the views are known to be stunning and you can look back and see how far you have come. Camp 4 is the highest camp on earth at 26,000 ft. It is known as the death zone. Humans struggle to survive unaided if they are unfamiliar with the altitude and need extra oxygen. Many get there and don’t make it to the summit. It is another 3000 ft to get to the top of Everest. The satisfaction when you get there must be immense, as only two-thirds of the climbers who set out actually reach the summit. 

 

How to climb your Everest  

 

Now while there is less altitude sickness when it comes to growing your business, there are a lot of similarities. The path to Everest is much like the path in business, you need the effort to be successful. Here are some of the lessons we can learn:  

 

  1. No one can reach the top of Everest without setting a goal. In your business, you need to set big goals and have an end destination in mind.  

 

  1. You need to build a good foundation before starting to climb. For a mountaineer that could take years of training and preparation. Planning and preparation can seem boring and feel like you are not getting anywhere, but planning and preparing and putting systems in place will really ensure you get where you want to go.  

 

  1. You really need to make a plan now on how you can reach your goal. The camps on Everest are where you can re-group and take stock before pushing to the next camp. Breaking a big goal down into stages means that you consistently take a few steps every day to the next step. Your journey seems more achievable, and you can make the changes you need to make gradually.  

 

  1. Don’t be afraid to ask for help. When climbing Everest, Sherpas are vital to guide climbers up the mountain. They have been there and done that, have a wealth of experience and know exactly where and when the challenges and dangers are. When in business you enter unknown territory, don’t be afraid to ask for help and get advice on how to tackle challenges in the right way. It can save you a lot of money in the long run. Coaches are a great resource and they can fast track you on the way to your goal, as they see past the day-to-day running of your business and can work out strategies to reach goals faster.  

 

  1. Remember the end goal isn’t the only significant achievement. Each time you reach a goal you need to celebrate and recognise that you need to stop every now and again and enjoy the journey. This could be just the psychological boost you need to get there. Goals can change, life can be surprising and it doesn’t always take goals into consideration. Maybe you need to stop and take a different track. Everest climbers sometimes have to change their goal if the weather or conditions change, but they have already achieved so much and it is worth celebrating. 

 

If you would like to make 2022 a standout year for you and your business feel free to get in touch and book a strategy call to see how we can help you transform your business here.

title.rendered: 5 Top Hack for Getting Off the Tools for Tradespeople

content.rendered:
Are you spending endless hours on the job site while your business growth takes a back seat? Many successful tradespeople reach a point where getting off the tools becomes crucial for scaling their business, yet they struggle with making this vital transition.

We understand this challenge because we’ve helped countless trade business owners make this exact journey. Whether you’re worried about maintaining quality standards, managing your team, or finding the right moment to step back, this comprehensive guide will show you how to transition from tradesman to business owner effectively.

In this guide, we’ll walk you through our proven framework for getting off the tools or stepping away from daily operations while ensuring your business continues to thrive. From assessing your readiness to building a self-running team, we’ll cover everything you need to know about getting off the tools and focusing on growing your business.

Assessing Your Readiness to Getting off the Tools

Before leaping getting off the tools, we need to ensure you’re truly ready for this significant transition. Recent data shows that 52% of tradespeople are experiencing lower profits than expected, making it crucial to time this transition correctly.

Financial indicators for transition

We’ve found that financial readiness is your first checkpoint. With current market conditions showing stability in repair and maintenance work (up 1%), while house building has decreased by 12%, it’s essential to evaluate your business’s financial health. Your business should demonstrate consistent profitability and stable cash flow before you consider stepping back.

Team capability assessment

Understanding your team’s capabilities is crucial for a successful transition. Our experience shows that the construction industry faces significant skills shortages, with 43% of businesses reporting delayed work due to lack of skilled workers. We recommend conducting a thorough capability assessment across three levels:

  • Direct reports and team leads
  • Key operational staff
  • Specialist skill holders

Personal preparation checklist

We’ve identified that successful transitions require more than just financial and team readiness. Your business should be prepared for exit from an early stage. Consider these essential elements:

  • Growth dynamics and market potential
  • Management team capabilities
  • Operational strengths
  • Governance processes and controls

Remember, everything required to prepare for getting off the tools is also essential for running an efficient and profitable business. This isn’t just about preparing to step away – it’s about building a stronger, more sustainable operation.

Creating Your Exit Strategy from Tools

Now that we’ve established your readiness to transition, let’s create a structured exit strategy that will help you successfully transition getting off the tools. Our experience shows that having a clear exit strategy from the early stages is crucial for business success.

Phased transition planning

We recommend implementing a gradual transition approach for getting off the tools and becoming a business owner. Start by identifying which tasks you can delegate first while maintaining quality control. Research shows that 90% of existing trade jobs have medium to highly transferable skills, making it easier to train your team effectively.

Client communication strategy

Clear client communication is vital during this transition period. We’ve found that overcommunication is better than leaving clients in the dark. Here are our proven communication principles:

  • Set clear expectations about timeline and costs upfront
  • Provide regular updates on work progress
  • Respond promptly to client inquiries
  • Document all agreements in writing

Timeline development

Developing a realistic timeline is crucial for a successful transition. Start by mapping out key milestones over a 6-12 month period. Your timeline should include specific dates for:

  • Gradual reduction of on-site work
  • Team training and development phases
  • Client relationship handover stages

Remember, research shows that having an exit strategy gives you clarity and direction for your business growth. We’ve seen that business owners who plan their exit strategy early are more likely to maintain quality standards and client satisfaction throughout the transition period.

Building a Self-Running Team

Building a successful self-running team is the cornerstone of getting off the tools effectively. We’ve found that over 80% of businesses that employ apprentices reported increased productivity, making this a crucial strategy for growth.

Recruitment best practises

In our experience, finding the right team members requires looking beyond just technical skills. When recruiting, we focus on these essential qualities:

  • Smart and ambitious candidates who demonstrate eagerness to learn
  • Team players who fit well with existing culture
  • Hard workers willing to go the extra mile

Training and development programmes

We’ve seen remarkable success with apprenticeship programmes, where 74% of companies report higher loyalty rates compared to traditional hires. Our approach to training includes structured development programmes that combine on-the-job training with formal education. This investment pays off – studies show that CEOs who excel at delegating generate 33% higher revenue.

Creating accountability systems

Creating effective accountability systems is crucial for transitioning from tradesman to business owner. We implement regular performance reviews and feedback loops to maintain quality. Our proven approach includes setting clear performance metrics, providing regular feedback, and encouraging ownership of work. This system helps create what we call “positive peer pressure,” where team members naturally strive to maintain high standards.

Remember, building a self-sufficient team takes time and patience. We’ve found that while a task might take you 30 minutes, it could take an hour for a new team member initially. However, this investment in people development is crucial for successfully getting off the tools and scaling your business.

Maintaining Quality Without Direct Involvement

Quality management becomes crucial when getting off the tools, and our research shows that poor quality can cost an average company 20% of their sales. Let’s explore how to maintain excellence without direct involvement.

Quality assurance frameworks

We’ve found that implementing robust quality management requires systematic documentation and clear processes. Our experience shows that successful quality frameworks should include:

  • Regular policy updates and clear escalation procedures
  • Systematic risk assessments
  • Pre-trade controls for credit limits
  • Independent evaluation of alerts
  • Comprehensive staff training programmes

Performance monitoring systems

In our work with trade businesses, we’ve seen that real-time monitoring is essential. We recommend implementing computerised management systems that analyse machine conditions and provide automated notifications. This approach helps identify potential issues before they affect production quality.

Customer feedback loops

Customer experience is paramount – 86% of consumers will pay more for better service. Here are our proven steps for implementing effective feedback loops:

  1. Collect targeted customer feedback through short-form surveys
  2. Analyse feedback data to identify patterns
  3. Apply insights to improve processes
  4. Follow up with customers directly
  5. Monitor improvements through continuous feedback

By implementing these systems, we’ve helped numerous trades businesses maintain high standards while successfully transitioning away from tools. Remember, quality assurance is an ongoing process, not a one-time setup.

Getting Off the Tools – Are You Ready?

Making the transition from hands-on tradesperson to business owner marks a crucial step in your business growth journey. Through proper planning, systematic team development, and robust quality management systems, you can successfully getting off the tools while maintaining your high service standards.

Success lies in careful preparation and timing. Your readiness assessment, structured exit strategy, and investment in team development will create a strong foundation for this transition. Many trade business owners who followed these steps now run thriving operations without daily hands-on involvement.

Remember that getting off the tools doesn’t mean stepping away from your business values. Quality management frameworks, performance monitoring, and customer feedback systems will help maintain your reputation for excellence. Your role shifts from doing the work to leading your team toward greater achievements.

This transition might feel challenging at first, but the long-term benefits make it worthwhile. A well-executed move from tradesperson to business owner opens new growth opportunities and creates a more sustainable future for your business.

title.rendered: 5 Best Tips How to Find Good Tradesmen-Avoid Dodgy Builders!

content.rendered:
We’ve all heard the horror stories. The dodgy builder who disappears with your deposit. The shoddy workmanship that needs to be redone (at your expense, of course). The endless delays that push your project months behind schedule. This leaves you feeling uneasy about how to find good tradesmen and the process can feel like navigating a minefield, especially for small to medium-sized construction businesses in the UK with limited resources.

But what if there was a way to avoid these pitfalls and a hack on how to find good tradesmen to help you build a network of skilled professionals you can trust? What if finding good tradesmen could become your secret weapon for delivering exceptional projects and scaling your business?

In this guide, we’ll reveal 5 expert tips on how to find good tradesmen and navigate the hiring process with confidence. You’ll learn how to identify your needs, explore diverse sourcing channels, conduct thorough vetting, and trust your instincts. Mastering how to find good tradesmen is crucial for avoiding those nightmares and ensuring your projects are built on a foundation of skill and reliability.

1. Define Your Needs: Laying the Foundation

Before you even start your search, it’s crucial to have a crystal-clear understanding of your needs and the project’s scope. Think of it as laying the foundation for a successful hiring process.

  • Project Scope: What exactly are you looking for? Are you building a new extension, renovating a property, or tackling a specialized project like a loft conversion? Define the specific trades involved (e.g., carpentry, electrical, plumbing) and the level of expertise required. Do you need a master craftsman or someone with basic skills for simpler tasks?
  • Project Timeline: When do you need the tradesmen to start? How long will the project last? Do you need someone for a short-term project, or are you looking for a long-term partnership? Being clear about your timeline will help you find tradesmen who are available and committed to your project schedule.
  • Budget: Let’s be realistic – budget matters. Establish a clear budget range for labour costs. This will help you narrow down your search and avoid wasting time on tradesmen whose rates are outside your affordability.

It’s best to create a project brief that outlines the key aspects of your undertaking. This document should include a description of the work to be done, any specific materials or techniques required, and your desired timeline. Understanding these factors is the first step in how to find good tradesmen who are the right fit for your project.

2. Explore Sourcing Channels: Cast a Wide Net

Gone are the days of relying solely on word-of-mouth or a dusty old directory. Today, there are a multitude of channels to help you find good tradesmen. Mastering how to find good tradesmen involves knowing where to look. Cast a wide net and explore these options:

  • Online Platforms: Embrace the digital age! Online platforms like Checkatrade, Rated People, and TrustMark are treasure troves of local tradesmen. These platforms offer a convenient way to browse profiles, read reviews, and compare quotes. Many even include photos of previous work, giving you a visual sense of the tradesperson’s skills and style.
  • Industry Associations: Knowing how to find good tradesmen also means understanding the importance of professional organizations. Contact relevant trade associations, such as the Federation of Master Builders or the Chartered Institute of Building, for recommendations or to access their directories of qualified members. These associations often have strict membership criteria, ensuring a certain level of quality and professionalism.
  • Word-of-Mouth Referrals: Never underestimate the power of personal recommendations. Ask your network – friends, family, colleagues, and even other businesses in the construction industry – for their suggestions. Word-of-mouth referrals can be a goldmine for finding trusted tradesmen who have already proven their worth.
  • Local Suppliers: Build relationships with local builders’ merchants and suppliers. They often have their finger on the pulse of the local tradesmen community and can provide valuable insights and recommendations.

3. Conduct Thorough Vetting: Essential Steps in How to Find Good Tradesmen

Finding good tradesmen is like finding a needle in a haystack. You need to be discerning, thorough, and willing to do your homework.

  • Check Qualifications and Experience: Don’t just take their word for it. Learning how to find good tradesmen goes beyond simply checking their qualifications and experience. Ask for proof of certifications, licenses, and insurance. Are they Gas Safe registered? Do they have the necessary NICEIC certifications? Make sure they have the credentials to back up their claims.
  • Review Portfolios and Testimonials: Seeing is believing. Examine their previous work. Ask for photos or, even better, visit completed projects if possible. Read online reviews and testimonials to get a sense of their quality and reliability. What do their past clients say about their work ethic, communication, and problem-solving skills?
  • Conduct Interviews: Don’t be afraid to ask the tough questions. Interview potential tradesmen to assess their communication skills, professionalism, and understanding of your project. Do they listen attentively to your needs? Can they clearly explain their approach to the work? Do they seem genuinely interested in your project?
  • Obtain Written Quotes: Get everything in writing. Obtain detailed written quotes from multiple tradesmen. Compare the quotes carefully, paying attention to not just the price but also the scope of work, materials included, and payment terms. A detailed quote shows professionalism and helps avoid misunderstandings down the line.

4. Trust Your Instincts: Your Gut Feeling Matters

Sometimes, it’s not just about the qualifications on paper. Trust your gut feeling. While qualifications and experience are important, trusting your instincts is also a key part of how to find good tradesmen who are a good fit for your company culture.

  • First Impressions Matter: Pay attention to how the tradesmen present themselves and communicate. Are they responsive, professional, and transparent? Do they show up on time for appointments? Do they answer your questions clearly and honestly? First impressions can reveal a lot about a person’s work ethic and reliability.
  • Red Flags: Be wary of tradesmen who are evasive, pushy, or unwilling to provide references or written quotes. Do they seem overly eager to secure the job without asking many questions? Do they pressure you to make a quick decision? Trust your gut feeling if something doesn’t seem right.
  • Open Communication: Once you’ve chosen a tradesman, establish clear expectations and maintain open communication throughout the project. Address any concerns promptly and professionally. A good working relationship is built on trust and mutual respect.

Remember, what’s a red flag for one person might not be for another. It’s perfectly normal not to perceive every negative trait as a problem. However, if something doesn’t feel right, trust your instincts. Bring up your concerns from your own point of view, sharing how their behaviour affects you is also important in how to find good tradesmen.

5. How to Find Good Tradesmen: The Power of Referrals

While online platforms and industry associations are valuable resources, understanding how to find good tradesmen often comes down to the power of personal recommendations. In a world of online reviews, a trusted referral can be worth its weight in gold.

  • Tap Your Network: Reach out to your network of friends, family, colleagues, and other businesses in the construction industry. Ask if they have any recommendations for reliable tradesmen they’ve worked with in the past. A personal endorsement can give you valuable peace of mind.
  • Qualify the Referral: When you receive a referral, don’t hesitate to ask questions. What type of project did they hire the tradesman for? Were they satisfied with the quality of work, communication, and adherence to deadlines? The more information you gather, the better equipped you’ll be to make an informed decision.
  • Online Reviews as Referrals: While not as personal as a direct recommendation, online reviews can also serve as a form of referral. Browse platforms like Checkatrade and Rated People to see what other clients have to say about their experiences with specific tradesmen. Look for patterns in the feedback – both positive and negative – to get a well-rounded perspective.

Build Your Dream Team

Finding good tradesmen is an investment in the success of your construction business. By implementing these 5 expert tips on how to find good tradesmen, you can build a reliable network of skilled professionals who will help you deliver exceptional projects, exceed client expectations, and achieve your growth ambitions. If you need help in a focus strategy on how to find good tradesmen, Develop Coaching course is designed to help business owners tread this minefield confidently.

Remember, it’s not just about finding someone to do the job; it’s about finding the right people who share your commitment to quality, efficiency, and professionalism. With careful planning, thorough vetting, and a bit of gut instinct, you can assemble a dream team of tradesmen who will become invaluable assets to your business.

title.rendered: Unbeatable USP for Construction Company – How to Stand Out

content.rendered:
In today’s competitive construction industry, standing out from the crowd is crucial for success. You might be wondering, “What is a USP and why does my construction company need one?” A unique selling proposition or USP for construction company is the secret weapon that can set your business apart and attract more clients. By identifying and showcasing what makes your company special, you’ll have a better chance to win projects and grow your business in a crowded market.

To develop a strong USP for a construction company, you’ll need to conduct thorough market research and perform a SWOT analysis. This will help you uncover your competitive advantage and craft a compelling value proposition. We’ll guide you through the process of identifying your unique strengths, creating a powerful USP, and putting it into action to showcase your company’s best qualities. By the end of this article, you’ll have the tools to create a USP that resonates with potential clients and gives your construction business the edge it needs to thrive.

Understanding the Concept of USP in Construction

In the competitive world of construction, standing out is crucial. A Unique Selling Proposition (USP) is your secret weapon to set your business apart. It’s that special quality or benefit that makes your company better than the rest. Think of it as your signature, guiding potential clients to choose you over others.

Your USP for construction company should be clear and easy to communicate. It’s not just about a specific product feature; it can encompass your entire organisation, from customer service to materials used. A strong USP helps define your place in the market, showcasing the specific benefits you offer that your competitors can’t match.

To develop a powerful USP, start with self-reflexion. Ask yourself what makes your construction company different. Consider your strengths, expertise, and unique approach to projects. Then, conduct thorough market research to understand your competitors and identify gaps you can fill.

Identifying Your Construction Company’s Unique Strengths

To uncover what makes your construction company special, you need to take a good look at your business. Start by doing a SWOT analysis. This helps you figure out your strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. Here are 5 simple steps that will help you identify USP for construction company:

  1. Identify your ideal client
    Understand who they are, their needs, and what motivates them.

  2. Pinpoint their key challenges
    Consider the specific problems or concerns they’re facing.

  3. Showcase your unique solution
    Clearly explain how you address their challenges in a way that stands out.

  4. Highlight your key benefits
    Emphasize the unique advantages your service or product offers.

  5. Offer a compelling promise
    Provide a guarantee or reassurance that builds trust and makes choosing you an easy decision.

Don’t forget to ask your clients what they think. Their feedback can show you what they value most about your services. This can help shape a USP that really speaks to your target audience. Also, check out what your competitors are up to. Look for gaps in the market that your company can fill. This will make your USP truly stand out.

Crafting a Compelling USP for Your Construction Business

Creating a powerful USP is essential for setting yourself apart from competitors. Focus on your unique strengths and what resonates with your target audience.

  • Are you known for sustainable practices or cutting-edge technology?
  • Highlight your team’s unmatched expertise or project management skills.
  • Emphasize efficient processes that reduce timelines or a commitment to exceeding quality standards.
  • For luxury homes, focus on attention to detail and premium materials.
  • For commercial projects, showcase your ability to deliver on time and within budget.
  • Ensure your USP is clear, concise, and memorable—it’s a promise you must consistently deliver.

Implementing and Showcasing Your USP

To make your USP shine, you need to weave it into every aspect of your business. Start by featuring it prominently in your marketing efforts. Your website, social media, and ads should all shout about what makes you special. Use real-life examples to back up your claims. Share success stories that show how you’ve delivered on your promises. This builds trust and sets you apart from the competition.

Don’t forget your team! Make sure they understand and embrace your USP. When everyone’s on the same page, you’ll create a consistent, customer-focused experience. Remember, your USP isn’t just words – it’s a promise you need to keep. Every interaction should reflect your unique qualities. By consistently delivering, you’ll build credibility and foster long-term relationships with your clients.

Conclusion on USP for Construction Company

Developing a strong USP for construction company has a significant impact on the success of your business. By pinpointing your unique strengths and crafting a compelling message, you’re setting yourself apart in a crowded market. This approach not only attracts more clients but also builds a solid foundation for long-term growth and success in the construction industry.

Remember, your USP isn’t just a catchy slogan – it’s a promise you make to your clients. To make it work, you need to weave it into every part of your business, from marketing to day-to-day operations. If you’d like to learn more about how to put strategies in place to grow your business, check out the Win Big Clients course from Develop Coaching. By consistently delivering on your unique value proposition, you’ll build trust, foster lasting relationships, and pave the way for your construction company to thrive in a competitive landscape.

title.rendered: 5 Hack – Customer Reviews for Construction Company

content.rendered:
Imagine this: a potential client is deciding between your company and a competitor. They’re comparing websites and services, but then they see your customer reviews. Suddenly, the decision is clear. Why? Because online testimonials are trusted endorsements that influence choices and build reputations. For ambitious construction companies, especially SMEs looking to grow, customer reviews for construction company is essential.


This article is your guide to making customer reviews work for you. We’ll explore how to gather feedback, showcase successes, and turn negative reviews into positive outcomes. Ready to unlock the potential of customer reviews for construction company and build a business that shines? Let’s dive in.

The Power of Customer Reviews for Construction Company

In construction, your reputation is your currency. Customer reviews for construction company are valuable endorsements that can boost your business. They’re digital word-of-mouth, influencing potential clients and shaping your online narrative.

But their impact goes beyond just “looking good”. Here’s how customer reviews for construction companies make a difference:

  • Build Trust and Credibility: In an industry where trust is highly valued, positive reviews act as powerful testimonials. Potential clients are more likely to choose a company with a proven track record. Reviews provide social proof, demonstrating that you deliver on promises and exceed expectations.
  • Boost Online Visibility: Google favours businesses with positive reviews. The more you have, the higher you’ll rank in local search results. This means increased visibility, making it easier for potential clients to find you. According to SEO practice, online reviews are a top local search ranking factor. If you want to dominate search results and attract more organic traffic, focus on generating those 5-star reviews.
  • Enhance Your Online Reputation: Customer reviews contribute to your online presence, painting a picture of your commitment to quality and customer satisfaction. Consistent positive feedback showcases your strengths and builds a strong online reputation, setting you apart.
  • Provide Valuable Feedback: Customer reviews are also a source of feedback. Pay attention to what your clients are saying. Their comments offer insights into what you’re doing well and where you can improve. This feedback is invaluable for refining your services and staying ahead.

Research by BrightLocal found that 91% of consumers read online reviews, and 84% trust them as much as personal recommendations. This highlights the influence of customer reviews on consumer behaviour. For construction companies, proactively managing your online reputation and generating positive reviews is a necessity.

Strategies for Collecting Customer Reviews for Construction Company

You’ve delivered exceptional work and thrilled your clients. Now, turn that satisfaction into valuable testimonials. How do you collect customer reviews for your construction company? Here’s a proactive approach:

Don’t Be Shy – Just Ask!

The most effective way to get reviews is to simply ask. Many satisfied clients are happy to share their experiences, but they might need a nudge. Make it standard practice to request feedback after every project.

  • Automate the Process: Streamline the process with an automated system. Use email marketing software or dedicated review platforms to send review requests automatically after project completion. This ensures consistency and frees up your time.
  • Optimise Timing: Timing is key. Send requests mid-week and in the morning for better response rates. Reach out while the experience is fresh in the client’s mind – the sooner you ask, the more likely they are to provide detailed feedback.
  • Provide Direct Links: Make it easy for clients to leave a review. Include direct links to your preferred platforms in your request. The fewer clicks involved, the better.

Focus on Quality, Not Just Quantity

While a high volume of reviews is beneficial, quality matters more. A handful of detailed testimonials can be more impactful than many generic ones.

  • Encourage Feedback After Positive Interactions: If a client expresses satisfaction, seize the opportunity to request a review.
  • Educate Clients on the Importance of Reviews: Explain how their reviews help you grow and improve your services. This can increase their willingness to share their experiences.

Leveraging Positive Reviews for Business Growth

Positive customer reviews for construction company are more than just a source of pride – they’re powerful marketing tools that can fuel your growth. Think of them as digital testimonials that sing your praises, attracting new clients and solidifying your reputation as a leader in the industry.

But how do you make the most of this valuable feedback? Here’s how to leverage positive reviews for maximum impact:

Showcase Reviews Across Multiple Channels

Don’t let your positive reviews gather dust in the depths of the internet! Shout them from the rooftops (or at least across your various online platforms). The more visible your reviews are, the more they’ll work in your favour.

  • Website: Your website is your online storefront, so make sure it showcases your best assets. Feature a slideshow of your most compelling customer reviews on your homepage to instantly capture attention. Create a dedicated testimonials page where you can share client stories and highlight specific projects. Include photos of your completed work alongside the reviews to create a visually engaging experience.
  • Social Media: Social media is a fantastic platform for sharing customer feedback and engaging with your audience. Regularly post positive reviews on your social media channels, and consider tagging the clients who left them (if they’re comfortable with it). Encourage interaction by asking your followers to share their own experiences with your company.
  • Email Marketing: Don’t forget about the power of email! Include customer testimonials in your email newsletters and marketing campaigns to build credibility and demonstrate the value you provide. A well-placed review can be just the thing to convince a potential client to choose your company.

Turn Satisfied Clients into Brand Advocates

Satisfied clients are your greatest asset. They’re not just customers – they’re potential brand advocates who can spread the word about your exceptional work.

  • Go Above and Beyond: Consistently exceeding client expectations is the foundation for generating positive reviews and fostering loyalty. When you go the extra mile, clients are more likely to sing your praises.
  • Engage with Reviewers: Don’t just passively receive reviews – engage with them! Respond to positive reviews with gratitude and personalised messages. This shows that you value their feedback, appreciate their business, and strengthens the client relationship.
  • Run Contests and Incentives: While adhering to platform guidelines, consider offering incentives for clients who leave reviews. Incentives can be a great way to encourage more clients to share their experiences.

By implementing these strategies, you’ll transform positive customer reviews for construction company into powerful marketing tools that drive business growth and solidify your position as a leader in the construction industry.

Handling Negative Customer Reviews for Construction Company

Let’s face it – no matter how hard you try, negative customer reviews for construction company are bound to happen occasionally. But don’t despair! Negative customer reviews for construction company aren’t necessarily a disaster. In fact, when handled correctly, they can even enhance your reputation and demonstrate your commitment to customer satisfaction.

Here’s how to navigate the sometimes choppy waters of negative feedback:

Respond Promptly and Professionally

The key to handling negative customer reviews for construction company is to respond quickly and professionally. Ignoring negative feedback or dismissing it defensively will only exacerbate the situation and damage your reputation.

  • Acknowledge the Issue: Start by thanking the reviewer for their feedback and acknowledging their concerns. This shows that you’re taking their comments seriously and are willing to listen.
  • Offer a Sincere Apology: Even if you don’t believe the company is entirely at fault, offer a sincere apology for any inconvenience or dissatisfaction caused. Empathy goes a long way in diffusing tension and demonstrating your commitment to customer satisfaction.
  • Take the Conversation Offline: Provide contact information (phone number or email address) and encourage the reviewer to reach out directly to discuss the issue further. This allows for a more personal and productive conversation.
  • Propose Solutions: Where appropriate, offer to make things right. This might involve offering a re-service, a partial refund, or another solution that addresses the client’s concerns. Demonstrating your willingness to go the extra mile can turn a dissatisfied client into a loyal one.

Turn a Negative into a Positive

While it might seem counterintuitive, negative reviews can actually present an opportunity to showcase your professionalism and commitment to customer service.

  • Demonstrate Your Commitment to Customer Satisfaction: By responding constructively to negative feedback, you show potential clients that you value their opinions and are dedicated to resolving issues. This builds trust and demonstrates your commitment to exceeding expectations.
  • Showcase Your Professionalism: A calm, measured response to criticism can actually boost your credibility. It shows that you’re able to handle challenging situations with grace and professionalism, which are valuable qualities in the construction industry.

Remember, how you handle negative customer reviews for construction company is just as important as how you generate positive ones. By responding effectively and demonstrating your commitment to customer satisfaction, you can turn a potentially damaging situation into a positive one.

Don’t Be Shy – Ask for Customer Reviews for Construction Company

Let’s face it – customer reviews for construction company are no longer just a “nice-to-have” – they’re a vital component of any successful marketing strategy, especially for construction companies. Whether you’re a small start-up or a well-established firm, these online testimonials can significantly impact your growth trajectory.

By actively collecting and leveraging customer reviews, you can:

  • Enhance your online presence: Boost your visibility in local search results and attract more organic traffic to your website.
  • Build trust with potential clients: Demonstrate your credibility and showcase your commitment to customer satisfaction.
  • Drive business growth: Attract new clients, increase conversions, and solidify your position as a leader in the construction industry.
  • Gain valuable insights: Gather feedback to improve your services and exceed client expectations.

Remember, the power of customer reviews for construction company lies in their ability to shape your company’s reputation and influence purchasing decisions. By focusing on exceptional service, proactively seeking feedback, and engaging with your clients, you can unlock the full potential of customer reviews for construction company and build a construction business that thrives.

So, don’t be shy – start asking for those customer reviews for construction company today!

title.rendered: How to get good reviews?

content.rendered:
So the big question is how do you get good reviews? Because everyone looks at reviews on the internet don’t they. We’ve got big global companies now like Amazon and Trip advisor who are really encouraging their customers to look at a review before they purchase, and it’s become second nature to us now online. 

 

When your clients are looking to purchase big ticket items, for example a home extension, a rewire or a new boiler, be under no illusions they, are going to be scrutinising your reviews. They want to have absolute confidence in their construction company or builders to do a good job. Reviews are one way to lead a successful business and in this two part series I will be looking at four things:  

 

  • 1.How to get good reviews 
  • 2.What review platforms should you be using 
  • 3.How to get your client to leave a review 
  • 4.What steps to take after a bad review 

 

In this blog post we will be looking at parts one and two, starting with;

 

How to get good reviews 

 

Firstly you need to make sure that your clients have a place to leave a review. To leave a review you have to make sure that your review settings are turned on, so double check today that these settings are up and running. People who are most strongly motivated generally to leave a review are those who are leaving a bad one because of a bad experience. So how do you get your customers to leave a 5 star review?  

 

When you know your customer is really happy with the result why not give them a short questionnaire with some questions on how they found your service. For example: What did they most like about your service? What did you do well? Where could you improve? This last question is a critical one because at this point the customer will be able to tell you how they really feel and you can find out if it is a five star review or not. This would then give you the opportunity to smooth things over if needed. If they say for example that they are not happy with the finished product, maybe they were unhappy that there was a delay, you can explain the reasons why that might have been. If there were areas you failed to deliver as a company, then this is your chance to make it up to them, maybe you can offer them a discount or a free gift. You will find in many cases if you follow that process, the customer will be happy to uplift your review and potentially give you a five star one even if the job didn’t go as planned. Because then they know you have done everything in your power to solve the problem and that’s often just what people want.  

 

What platforms should you be getting a review on?

 

There are so many platforms it’s hard to know what will bring you the better business. Well if resources are tight and you carry out a business that is not naturally going to get lots of reviews every month, it may be best to start with one or two and then build it out. Now one of the best places to focus on reviews is Google as it’s the first port of call when someone searches your business, and any good reviews come up on your google ranking. Another great place to start is Facebook, I think the last time I checked it was about 2.8 billion users around the world and it’s probably much more than that now, it’s not a platform to be ignored. It’s easy to set up a Facebook business page and get your clients to leave reviews there. And then in construction there are many specialist sites out there, you have sites like Trustpilot, Trustatrader, Mybuilder, Federation Of Master Builders or Checkatrade. Don’t forget Yell, it still ranks highly on google and that is where your reviews will show generally on the first page.  

 

So in conclusion this year reviews are an important way to get business. It’s the best way to stand out above your competitors. Everyone looks at reviews so don’t ignore the power of them. In part two we will be looking at how you can ask your customers for reviews, and also what to do if you get a dreaded bad review.
