title.rendered: How To Find Your USP

content.rendered:
Every business needs one if they want to survive. In this article I will be discussing what a USP is and why you need one and I will answer the following 4 questions: 

  • What Does USP stand for? 
  • What is a USP? 
  • Why Do I Need a USP? 
  •  How can I create the best USP for my business? 

 

What Does USP stand for? 

 

USP stands for Unique Selling Point.

 

What is a USP? And Why Do I Need one? 

 

 A USP is what makes you stand out from the crowd. Most service firms will claim that they offer a great product. What’s going to make you different to the others?  The reality is, if you have nothing unique to offer you will be competing solely on price – this is the worst position to be in.  

 It may work in other industries, like discounted retailers (Aldi, Lidl) who sell products cheap but in huge quantities, but it’s not an effective strategy in the construction industry.  

 Competing on price may get you through the early days of a start-up, when overheads are low, but as you start to expand you will require staff, offices, equipment, computers, etc. When overheads increase significantly you will find that your prices have to rise  just to stay afloat.  

 The problem is, your clients will not care about your overheads. When they are given a price for a service, if someone else is delivering the same product at a cheaper price then you can almost guarantee you’ve lost that sale. 

 It’s imperative that you stand out, but that’s easier said than done.  Construction is a crowded industry and unless you’re offering a unique, specialist product that the average Joe isn’t, standing out will be a challenge. 

 But you can still stand out, even if you do not have a unique product.

 

Let’s take Apple as an example. 

They can sell a mobile phone for upwards of £1,000 when their rival Nokia can only charge £350 for their most expensive phone, which has many similar features. 

Even though Apple’s product is triple the price, they will outsell Nokia time and time again and are hugely profitable.  

Why? It’s not that they have a unique product, as the Nokia phone is almost the same. Apple has developed a way to stand head and shoulders above the competition. They have managed to develop branding and a reputation that makes it cool to be seen with an Apple phone. They also offer an exceptional service in their stores, providing a unique experience that helps drive sales and inspire customer loyalty.  

 Your construction company is nothing like Apple, though, so why mention it? The point is, you don’t have to be selling completely unique products to stand out from the crowd, and just because you are in a crowded marketplace, you still need to avoid being reliant on competing on price only. 

You’ll notice that companies all around you struggle with USP, as they all seem to offer the same benefits.  Some of the generic USPs you can find in the service industry include:

  • ‘Good quality and low prices’ 
  • ‘Affordable quality since 1990’ 
  • ‘Service with a smile’
  • ‘Satisfaction guaranteed’ 
  • ‘You’ve tried the rest, now try the best’ These are just taglines and certainly not unique, so don’t deserve to be called USPs. Phrases like this are commonplace in the market and are not going to differentiate you in any way, shape or form.

 

How can I find a USP for my construction company? 

 

One of the first things you need to focus on is your offer. What is the service or product you are offering to your clients, and, more importantly, why is it better than others? Are you able to articulate that? Can you pitch your product and explain why someone should use you in a confident and convincing way?

 

It is possible to stand out, but it involves having a clear understanding of your USP (unique selling proposition/point). It can sometimes take an outsider to help look objectively at a business. As a construction business coach that has built up years of experience in the industry, I can help you discover what makes you stand out as a construction company. Get in contact here to talk to me about how you can stand out from the crowd. Or if you are not ready to do that then read on to see how you can start to access what makes your business different.

 

It needs Exceptional Service to be good enough to differentiate you.  You need to be able to deliver on it.  You want to ensure it will make your clients choose you over the rest. If you want to see significant and sustained growth then exceptional service must become a core value within your business.  It must be the number one priority for you and your staff, and it needs to be constantly reaffirmed.  Without exceptional service, your company will be propped up by expensive marketing efforts, cheaper price points and new business only, which leaves you with low profitability. The easiest way to make a profit is to sell again to existing clients and those to whom you have been recommended, but the only way you’ll achieve this consistently is if you’re offering a great service.  

 

In order to offer a great service one of the first things needed is to understand who your client is, who you are selling to. What are their problems, fears and needs? You will attract the types of clients you focus on, so if you don’t like your current crop of clients, maybe it’s time to focus on selling to the ones you do want (provided you can deliver effectively to them).  

 Going forward, design your marketing strategy to attract only your ideal clients. Do the following as an exercise. First, start by writing down who your ideal client is. Be as detailed as you can. Create an avatar of that person. Ask questions like: 

  • What’s their age?  
  • Where do they live?  
  • How much do they earn?  
  • Are they single or married?  
  • Do they have children?  
  • What are their interests?  
  • What magazines do they read?  
  • What Facebook groups will they visit?  

 

Once you’ve worked out who that individual is, start thinking about how they think and feel: 

  • What are their wants?  
  • What are their needs?  
  • What are their worries?  
  • What problems do they have that need solving?  
  • What are they frustrated with in your industry?  

Once you start building up this picture it can help you formulate what your USP needs to be to appeal to and reach this individual.  Try to be as specific as you can and don’t fall into the trap of trying to be all things to all people. You will have more success focusing on a specific or niche market.  

Next, think about what your company does or can do that might be different to your competitors.  

  • What are your strengths and company values?  
  • Are you faster than others?  
  • Do you offer better quality?  
  • Have you been established a long time? 

 

Let’s take an example below:

The AA (Automobile Association): ‘To our members, we’re the fourth emergency service.’ 

 This USP again talks to customers’ fears. For someone vulnerable, it would be a nightmare for their car to break down on the side of a motorway. The AA reassures them that they will come to save them like a knight in shining armour. 

Even after working through the above steps, it can take some time to settle on something that fits. For assistance, why not ask previous clients what they thought was great about you? What were they worried about before they purchased your product or service? It’s a great way of getting into the mind of your ideal client – just ask them directly. Once you find your USP it will be liberating and give you direction and clarity on how to move forward.  Now you need to let everyone know what your USP is. I will discuss this in future articles. 

 

Conclusion 

 The construction industry is tough at the moment, but you CAN not only survive it but thrive in it.

title.rendered: How to Deal With Negative/Bad Reviews

content.rendered:
I discussed in a recent article how to get good reviews, if you missed it, you can catch up on it here  We briefly touched on dealing with negative reviews but in this article, I am going to focus on the bad or negative reviews. 

 

I will discuss: 

  1. How to view them 
  2. How to avoid bad reviews 
  3. How to learn from bad reviews 
  4. How to respond to bad/negative reviews 
  5.  

You’ve worked hard to build up your reputation and brand in your market. You’ve got some amazing reviews online and then, all of a sudden, someone posts something negative.  

There’s nothing more painful than a bad review and, although you may have plenty of good ones, the bad one will stand out like a sore thumb. Sometimes it’s unavoidable, as you’ll never please every single client – some jobs will go wrong.  

The danger arises if you start noticing poor reviews on a frequent basis.  

As you expand, the personal service you once offered will inevitably be affected.  

 

At first, your clients know you and only you, but as the business grows, you may become faceless. Your client only knows your company and feels no loyalty to you as an individual.  

Once the personal aspect has gone from the service offering, clients are less likely to put up with minor annoyances. You may have got away with these previously, as clients tend to overlook issues when dealing with an individual, but now you’re a faceless company they will feel they have a right to, at best, have a moan if things go wrong, or at worst, compensation or a scathing review.  

It’s important to recognise that this is the reality if you are going to scale up, so it’s imperative you keep your personal brand at the head of the business.  

 

One way to do this is to create and publish plenty of online blogs and vlogs so clients still know who you are.  

Visit a client’s project now and then, on a random basis. This means a lot to your client and shows that you take a personal interest.  

Sam Walton, the owner of Walmart, was declared the richest man in America in 1985. He insisted on regularly visiting his stores and getting down to the storefront, promoting goods himself. He loved it; the business was his baby. More importantly, though, he was ensuring he didn’t become a faceless company. People would see him, staff and customers, and he gave the impression that he genuinely cared about his business. He could have sat in a large office all day, but he ensured at least some of his time was spent on the shop floor.  

Do the same with your business even as you expand, and note that it goes a long way.  

Doing this will ensure you’re able to monitor the service you are giving to clients – you’ll be able to see it first-hand. If you notice things going wrong, or the service becoming poor, you can act quickly before the reviews are posted. 

 

The other thing to bear in mind is your reaction when a bad review appears. 

First, don’t overreact in anger. Often, you’ll want to reply immediately to defend yourself or ‘have a go’ back. But take your time and calm down before you respond, and then keep it professional.  

Apologise and acknowledge your client’s feelings and let them know that you’re looking into how to improve that area of the business. End your response positively, without making it look like you are dismissing the complaint. When potential clients see a response like this, they can sense you genuinely care, which can help with future sales.  

 

Replying to a Bad Review  

Here’s a great example of a reply to a bad review: 

‘Dear [use first name to be more personal]. Thank you for taking the time to leave a review. I apologise on behalf of everyone here at [insert company name]. Please know that your situation was an exception. As you can see from our other reviews, we care deeply about our customers and strive to deliver an outstanding service. We can’t fix the past but you have my personal commitment to improve the way our staff serves every customer. Until then, please accept my sincerest apologies on behalf of everyone on the team.’  

Don’t let the bad review knock you too much. Remember, it’s just an obstacle in the road, one that you can easily get around. Learn from it, use it as an opportunity to improve and then keep travelling towards your destination. 

 

Whilst you don’t want to ponder and wallow too much in negative review do a mini investigation into each and every negative review or complaint. Ask yourself: 

Could this have been prevented? 

Does the customer have a point? 

How would I feel if I was in their shoes? 

What should we have done differently? 

And the most important one 

  • What process can we add in our procedure to ensure this does not happen again?

 

Conclusion 

As you expand your business, there will be teething problems and sometimes service can slip, so keep on top of it. If you do start to receive some negative reviews, learn from them, deal with them in the right way and make the relevant changes so that your business remains ahead of the game.

title.rendered: Finding Skilled Tradesmen: Tips to Hire the Best

content.rendered:
Are you struggling to find skilled tradesmen for your latest project? You’re not alone. Finding skilled tradesmen in the trades that are reliable and competent can be a real challenge, especially in today’s competitive job market. Whether you’re looking to hire electricians, plumbers, carpenters, or other skilled workers, the process can often feel like searching for a needle in a haystack.

But don’t worry, we’ve got you covered. In this article, we’ll share some valuable tips to help you in finding skilled tradesmen who can meet your needs. We’ll explore how to define your requirements clearly, tap into your professional network, assess soft skills, and set up an effective screening process. By the end, you’ll be better equipped to recruit top-notch tradespeople who can contribute to your project’s success and support your company’s growth.

Define Your Requirements

To find skilled tradesmen, you need to be clear about what you’re looking for. Start by writing a brief that outlines your project’s specifics. Include measurements, architect plans, materials, finishes, and any fixtures or fittings you have in mind. This helps tradespeople understand your needs and expectations.

Consider the qualifications required for the job. Some trades don’t have formal entry requirements, while others need specific certifications. For example, gas engineers must be Gas Safe registered, and electricians often need Part P certification for domestic work.

Think about the level of experience you need. Time served in a trade is a good indicator of skill. Ask potential hires how long they’ve been in the trade and get them to explain their approach to the job. This can reveal their expertise and problem-solving abilities.

Utilise Your Network

Your network is a goldmine for finding skilled tradesmen. Start by asking your employees about their favourite past coworkers or anyone they know with the right skills. After all, 45% of job seekers hear about opportunities from friends! Don’t stop there – chat with friends, family, old school mates, and industry contacts from previous projects. They might know someone perfect for the job.

Local suppliers are another great resource. They talk to tradespeople daily, so let them know you’re hiring. Leave a few copies of your job ad with them – they might put it up for you!

Social media is your friend here. Post your job ad regularly on Facebook, Twitter, and LinkedIn. Don’t be shy about asking people to share it on their profiles. The more eyes on it, the better!

Evaluate Soft Skills

When finding skilled tradesmen, don’t overlook soft skills. A study by LinkedIn found that 92% of professionals believe soft skills are equally or more important than technical skills. These include communication, teamwork, and problem-solving abilities.

To assess these skills, observe how candidates interact during interviews. Look for clear communication, active listening, and adaptability. Ask about their experiences working in teams and handling conflicts. You can also present scenarios to see how they’d approach challenges on the job.

Remember, strong soft skills indicate a tradesperson’s ability to adapt, learn quickly, and contribute to long-term goals. By evaluating both technical and soft skills, you’re more likely to find tradesmen who’ll excel in their roles and help your projects succeed.

Implement Effective Screening

To find skilled tradesmen, you need a robust screening process. Start by thoroughly reviewing CVs, looking for relevant experience and qualifications. Plan your interview questions carefully, focusing on their achievements and reasons for job changes. During the interview, use a structured approach. Begin with a warm introduction, then ask the candidate to share their experience and interests. Listen attentively to their responses, as the details often reveal valuable insights.

Include behavioural questions to assess how they handle workplace challenges. For example, ask about a time they made a mistake or dealt with a difficult colleague. This helps gauge their problem-solving skills and attitude. Don’t forget to allow time for their questions too.

Finding Skilled Tradesmen Now

Finding skilled tradesmen can be a tough job, but with the right approach, it becomes much easier. By clearly defining your requirements, tapping into your network, evaluating soft skills, and setting up a solid screening process, you’ll be well on your way to hiring top-notch tradespeople. These steps help you find workers who not only have the technical know-how but also fit well with your team and project needs.

In the end, the effort you put into finding the right tradesmen has a big impact on your project’s success. It’s not just about filling a position; it’s about building a team that can tackle challenges, work well together, and deliver quality results. So take your time, follow these tips, and you’ll be more likely to find tradesmen who’ll help your business thrive and grow.

title.rendered: Unlock Successful Digital Marketing for Construction 2025

content.rendered:
Did you know that over 90% of construction projects start with online research? In today’s digital age, a strong online presence is no longer a luxury for construction companies – it’s a necessity. If you’re ready to revolutionise your business and attract more clients in 2025, mastering digital marketing for construction is essential.

The building industry is experiencing a significant shift, with online strategies playing a pivotal role in attracting clients, showcasing projects, and staying ahead of the competition. Embracing digital marketing for construction can have a transformative impact on your business, helping you to reach new heights and build a stronger foundation for success.

In this article, we’ll guide you through the essentials of digital marketing for construction companies. You’ll discover how to:

  • Create a compelling website that showcases your expertise.
  • Harness the power of SEO to improve your online visibility.
  • Leverage social media marketing to connect with potential clients.
  • Implement effective email marketing and lead generation strategies.
  • Explore paid advertising options to boost your reach.
  • The importance of local SEO for construction businesses.

By the end, you’ll be well-equipped to use digital marketing for construction to navigate the digital landscape and achieve your business goals.

Embracing Digital Transformation in Construction

In today’s rapidly evolving construction landscape, embracing digital marketing for construction is no longer optional—it’s essential for your success. As you navigate this new era, you’ll find that digital marketing for construction solutions has the power to revolutionise your operations, boost productivity, and give you a competitive edge.

The Importance of Digital Marketing for Construction Company

Digital marketing has become crucial for construction companies to enhance visibility and brand awareness. Most of your potential clients now begin their search for services online, making a strong digital presence vital. By implementing strategies like search engine optimisation, social media marketing, and targeted advertising, you can reach your desired audience more effectively than ever before.

Overcoming Industry Challenges

The construction industry faces unique challenges, including resistance to change and fragmented workflows. To overcome these hurdles, focus on fostering a culture of collaboration and change within your organisation. Engage stakeholders at all levels in the digital transformation process, emphasising how these solutions can streamline processes and enhance productivity.

Adopting New Technologies

To stay ahead, you need to invest in scalable solutions that adapt to your organisation’s needs. Consider technologies like AI, data analytics, and cloud management software. These tools can help you make faster decisions, improve cost control, and ultimately achieve higher project success rates. Remember, digital transformation isn’t just about new tools—it’s about a cultural shift towards progress and efficiency in your construction business.

Building a Strong Digital Foundation

To master digital marketing for construction in 2025, you need to build a strong digital foundation. This involves creating a user-friendly website, implementing SEO best practises, and establishing a social media presence.

Creating a User-Friendly Website

Within the digital marketing for construction world, your website is your digital storefront. It should be easy to navigate, mobile-friendly, and showcase your projects effectively.

  • Showcase your work: Use high-quality images and videos to highlight your projects, providing detailed descriptions and client testimonials whenever possible.
  • Optimise for user experience: Ensure your website is easy to navigate, with a clear menu structure and prominent calls to action (e.g., “Get a Quote,” “Contact Us”).
  • Prioritise mobile responsiveness: With more and more people accessing the internet on their smartphones, your website must be mobile-friendly to provide a positive user experience.

Make your website a priority and turn it into a powerful lead-generation tool for your construction business.

Implementing SEO Best Practises

Search Engine Optimisation (SEO) is crucial for improving your online visibility and attracting organic traffic to your website.

  • Keyword Research: Conduct thorough keyword research to identify the terms your potential clients are using to search for construction services.
  • On-Page Optimisation: Optimise your website’s content and structure with relevant keywords, compelling title tags, and informative meta descriptions.
  • Local SEO: Focus on local SEO by claiming and optimising your Google My Business profile, building local citations, and encouraging customer reviews.

Effective SEO ensures your construction company gets found by the right people at the right time.

Establishing Social Media Presence

Social media is a powerful tool for construction companies to connect with potential clients and build brand awareness.

  • Choose the right platforms: Focus on platforms where your target audience is most active, such as LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram.
  • Share engaging content: Showcase your projects, share industry insights, and post behind-the-scenes updates to keep your audience engaged.
  • Be consistent: Maintain a regular posting schedule and interact with your followers to build brand trust and recognition.

Ultimately, a strong social media presence helps you connect with your audience and build a thriving online community.

Advanced Digital Marketing Techniques

Laying a strong foundation is crucial, but to truly excel in the digital marketing for construction world, you need to go beyond the basics. Think of these advanced techniques as the strategies that will elevate your construction business to new heights, allowing you to reach a wider audience, generate more leads, and ultimately win more projects. Let’s explore some of the most effective advanced techniques in digital marketing for construction companies.

Tested Content Marketing Strategies

Create valuable, relevant content that addresses your audience’s needs and challenges.

  • Showcase your expertise: Share project showcases, case studies, and client testimonials to demonstrate your capabilities.
  • Educate your audience: Publish blog posts, articles, and guides on relevant construction topics to establish your company as a thought leader.
  • Use diverse formats: Engage your audience with various content formats, including blog posts, videos, infographics, and downloadable resources.

When you consistently deliver high-quality content, you can attract new clients, build brand loyalty, and drive business growth. 

Supplement with Paid Advertising Campaigns

While organic strategies like SEO and content marketing are essential, paid advertising can give your construction business a powerful boost. Pay-per-click (PPC) advertising allows you to put your company directly in front of potential clients who are actively searching for construction services online.

Platforms like Google Ads and Bing Ads offer highly targeted advertising options. You can bid on relevant keywords related to your services, ensuring your ads appear at the top of search results pages when potential clients are looking for companies like yours.

To maximise your return on investment (ROI), carefully set your budget, choose relevant keywords that align with your services, and create compelling landing pages that encourage visitors to take action. With careful planning and optimisation, paid advertising can be a highly effective way to generate leads and win new projects.

Email Marketing Automation 

Email marketing is far from outdated. It’s a powerful tool for building relationships and keeping your construction company top-of-mind with potential clients. With email automation, you can nurture leads over time and deliver targeted messages that resonate with their specific needs.

Start by building your email list organically. Offer valuable content upgrades, such as guides, checklists, or exclusive project insights, in exchange for email subscriptions. Then, segment your audience into groups based on their interests and needs, allowing you to tailor your messaging for maximum impact.

Use automated email sequences to nurture your leads with valuable information, share exciting project updates, and subtly promote your services. Think of it as staying in touch and building rapport, rather than bombarding them with sales pitches.

Measuring and Analysing Results

In the world of digital marketing for construction, data is king. Tracking and analysing your results is crucial to understand what’s working and what’s not. By monitoring key metrics, you can gain valuable insights into your audience and campaign performance, allowing you to make informed decisions and optimise your strategies for continuous improvement.

Keep a close eye on metrics such as:

  • Website traffic: How many visitors are coming to your website? Where are they coming from (e.g., search engines, social media, referrals)?
  • Leads generated: How many enquiries are you receiving through your website or other digital channels?
  • Conversion rates: What percentage of your website visitors are taking desired actions, such as filling out a contact form or requesting a quote?
  • Customer acquisition cost: How much does it cost you to acquire a new customer through your digital marketing efforts?

Leverage tools like Google Analytics to gather this data and understand user behaviour on your website. Regularly review your data and make adjustments to your strategies to optimise your results and achieve your business goals. Remember, digital marketing for construction is an ongoing process of refinement and improvement.

Ready to Implement Digital Marketing for Construction in Your Business?

As we’ve discussed, digital marketing will have a profound impact on the construction industry in 2024. By embracing the transformation in digital marketing for construction, building a strong online presence, and using advanced marketing techniques, construction companies can reach new heights. This approach not only boosts visibility but also helps to build trust with potential clients and stay ahead of the competition.

To wrap up, mastering digital marketing for construction isn’t just about using new tools; it’s about changing how we think about connecting with clients and growing our businesses. By putting these strategies into action, construction companies can build a stronger foundation for success in the digital age. Remember, the key is to keep learning and adapting as technology and marketing trends continue to evolve.

title.rendered: How to Dominate in the Social Media Construction Industry: 3 Proven Keys

content.rendered:
Have you ever wondered how social media is transforming the construction industry? In today’s digital age, platforms like Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and YouTube are reshaping how construction companies connect with clients, showcase their work, and grow their businesses. The social media construction industry revolution is in full swing, offering opportunities for companies to stand out in a competitive market. Sound intimidating? It shouldn’t be. In this article, you’ll discover the powerful impact of social media marketing on construction businesses. We’ll explore effective strategies to leverage these platforms for lead generation and brand building. You’ll learn how to measure your social media success and get inspiring social media ideas tailored for the construction industry. Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just starting out, following these tips will help you take advantage of social media to bring your construction business to the next level.

Social Media in the Construction Industry: A Powerful Tool for Growth

The Impact of Social Media on the Construction Industry

Social media has become a game-changer for construction companies, offering a powerful platform to connect with clients, showcase projects, and grow businesses. With over 56.2 million social media users in the UK alone, construction companies have an unprecedented opportunity to reach a vast audience and transform their marketing efforts. This means that effectively leveraging the social media construction industry is no longer optional, but essential for reaching new clients and staying competitive.

Increasing Brand Visibility

By embracing social media in the construction industry, companies can significantly expand their reach and attract more clients. Consistent posting across relevant platforms helps keep your brand top-of-mind, allowing you to communicate your expertise and unique selling points in a direct and accessible way. In an industry often built on reputation and trust, this increased visibility leads to greater brand awareness, which, in turn, translates to business growth. Additionally, social media provides an avenue for construction companies to showcase their values—whether it’s quality workmanship, sustainable building practices, or a commitment to safety—which can resonate with potential clients looking for these attributes in a partner.

Showcasing Project Portfolio

Social media provides an excellent platform to highlight your achievements and demonstrate your capabilities to a broad audience. With visual platforms like Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn, construction companies can share high-quality photos and videos of ongoing projects, leveraging before-and-after shots and even time-lapse videos to document the full scope of their work. This type of content helps potential customers gain confidence in your abilities, as they can see real examples of your skills and expertise. More importantly, showcasing completed projects helps differentiate your company from competitors by highlighting your distinct approach and successful outcomes. This attracts potential customers and strengthens your brand’s authority within the social media construction industry.

Engaging with Potential Clients

Social media isn’t just a place to broadcast information—it’s a place to engage in meaningful interactions with clients and prospects. Through platforms like LinkedIn and Twitter, you can participate in industry discussions, share valuable insights, and foster relationships with key players in your field. Sharing client testimonials and success stories offers a powerful form of social proof, reinforcing your credibility. Additionally, offering behind-the-scenes content allows followers to gain a deeper understanding of your processes, your team, and the company culture. This transparency builds trust and rapport with your audience. Engaging with followers also opens the door for direct communication, where prospective clients can ask questions or discuss potential projects.

Effective Social Media Strategies for Construction Companies

To fully harness the power of social media construction industry, businesses need to focus on three core areas: choosing the right platforms, creating engaging content, and maintaining a consistent posting schedule. When effectively implemented, these strategies help construction companies not only increase visibility but also build stronger relationships with clients and stakeholders, ultimately leading to long-term success in a competitive market.

Choosing the Right Platforms

Selecting the appropriate platforms is crucial for your success. For visually driven content like project photos, time-lapse videos, and before-and-after shots, Instagram, with its 1.628 billion users, is an ideal choice. It allows you to showcase the high-quality craftsmanship and innovative techniques your company employs. Similarly, Facebook—with its massive 2.9 billion monthly active users—offers excellent opportunities for brand recognition, community engagement, and sharing company milestones. LinkedIn should also be considered, as it offers a more professional environment for B2B engagement, networking with industry leaders, and sharing thought leadership content. By choosing one or two platforms that align with your business objectives and the preferences of your target audience, you can maximise the effectiveness of your social media construction industry efforts while avoiding the risk of spreading your resources too thin across multiple platforms.

Creating Engaging Content

Creating varied and engaging content is essential for capturing your audience’s attention. Use a mix of content types, such as before-and-after images to showcase transformations, behind-the-scenes glimpses of your team and processes, and how-to videos that highlight your expertise. Client testimonials are crucial for building trust and credibility—share these to demonstrate successful projects and happy clients. Additionally, relevant hashtags can help increase your visibility and reach within the construction sector. Storytelling is a powerful tool to create an emotional connection with your audience. Narrate the challenges you’ve overcome in your projects, the innovative solutions you’ve implemented, and the benefits your clients have experienced. This approach makes your content more engaging and helps potential clients understand the value you bring to their projects.

Consistency in Posting

Maintain a regular posting schedule to keep your audience engaged and signal to social media algorithms that your account is active. Aim for 3-5 posts per week on Facebook and consider more frequent posts on platforms like Twitter. Consistency builds trust and keeps your brand top-of-mind with followers, a key factor in the social media construction industry.

Measuring Social Media Success in the Construction Industry

To measure the impact of your social media construction industry efforts, you need to focus on key performance indicators (KPIs) that align with your business goals. Start by tracking website traffic and leads generated from social media using tools like Google Analytics. Monitor engagement rates and follower growth to assess your content’s effectiveness. Analyse the sentiment of comments and reviews to address feedback promptly. Conduct surveys to measure customer satisfaction and brand perception. By regularly evaluating these metrics, you can make data-driven decisions to optimise your strategy and maximise your social media success in the construction industry.

Final Takeaway: Use of Social Media Construction Industry

Social media construction industry has reshaped the game of marketing, providing companies with new ways to connect with clients, showcase their work, and grow their businesses. Platforms like Instagram and Facebook offer unparalleled opportunities to boost visibility, display your project portfolio, and engage directly with potential customers. The key to success lies in selecting the right platforms, crafting engaging content, and maintaining a consistent presence. By carefully measuring your social media efforts with focus on KPI and refining your approach, you can unlock new growth opportunities within the social media construction industry. Social media is more than just a marketing tool—it’s a powerful way to build relationships, demonstrate expertise, and elevate your business in the digital age. Happy socialising!

FAQs

How is social media utilised within the construction sector?

Marketing for the social media construction industry involves utilising platforms to promote their services, display their projects, and interact with potential customers and the wider community. This strategy is particularly beneficial for construction companies due to the visually compelling nature of their work.

What strategies can construction companies employ to leverage social media effectively?

Construction companies should highlight client reviews and testimonials. Ensure your construction services are commendable and encourage clients to post reviews. Sharing testimonials on your social media channels can also help to establish trust and credibility amongst your audience. Never underestimate the impact of positive feedback!

What function does social media serve in contemporary communication?

Social media has transformed personal communication, supplanting traditional methods like letters and phone calls. It challenges conventional language rules concerning expression creativity, politeness, relationships, and confessions, reflecting its broad influence on modern communication.

How does social media contribute to the development of a positive body image?

When used healthily, social media can support the promotion of body positivity by encouraging the sharing of unaltered, non-sexualised images of diverse body types. This fosters an environment of self-love and acceptance, highlighting the platform’s potential for positive influence.

title.rendered: How to Stop Wasting Time on Quotes: 5 Best Practises

content.rendered:
Construction professionals dedicate 15 hours every week to prepare quotes – that’s almost two full working days of work!

Most of us know the familiar scenario. The endless back-and-forth emails never stop. Project details go missing. Customers keep changing their minds. These time-consuming activities in the construction industry drain your productivity and affect your profits significantly.

Your time gets buried in paperwork while creating detailed estimates for materials and labour. This valuable time could help you win new projects or manage existing ones effectively. A better solution exists to handle construction quotes without letting difficult customers disrupt your schedule.

If you’re looking for ways on how to stop wasting time on quotes, you’re in the right place. Your quoting process needs a transformation from a time-sink into a simplified operation. These proven strategies will help you save time on quotes and focus on what truly matters – growing your business.

Streamline Your Quote Request Process

Making your quote request process better requires well-defined systems and procedures. Companies that use standard quoting processes see better efficiency and customer satisfaction rates. To stop wasting time on quotes, start by refining how you handle quote requests.

Creating Clear Quote Requirements

A detailed catalogue of your products or services with descriptions and pricing should be your starting point. These are the foundations of accurate quotes that help prevent future confusion. You need a clear pricing structure with fixed prices for different service tiers that reflect project complexity. Your requirements should include:

  • Company details and branding
  • Customer information fields
  • Product/service descriptions
  • Pricing and payment terms
  • Delivery timeframes
  • Terms and conditions

Standardising Quote Request Forms

Poor usability causes more than 50% bounce rate in most forms. Your quote request forms should have larger field sizes and only necessary information fields to prevent this. The forms should highlight missing information right away through automatic field corrections, which helps customers complete them correctly. This is another crucial step in learning how to stop wasting time on quotes.

Setting Realistic Deadlines

The right deadlines play a vital role in managing quote requests well. Smaller quotes need at least two weeks of preparation time, while complex projects require more. Extra time for unexpected changes or revisions should be included. This approach reduces stress and lets you deliver quotes early, which impresses potential clients.

Note that tracking responses as they arrive and quick acknowledgment keeps your quote process running smoothly. This shows your prospects how professional you are and another step in how to stop wasting time on quotes.

Leverage Technology for Quote Management

Modern technology provides powerful solutions that can revolutionise your quote management process. Quote automation software such as Xero helps you generate accurate, professional quotes in minutes instead of hours. Understanding how to stop wasting time on quotes means embracing the power of technology.

Quote Management Software Solutions

Your business can benefit from configure-price-quote (CPQ) software that combines smoothly with your existing systems. These solutions pull data from multiple sources, including your CRM, product catalogues, and pricing databases to create highly accurate quotes. Quote automation reduces your overall quote-to-cash process time and delivers tangible business gains.

Automation Tools and Templates

Your quoting process becomes better with automation tools that:

  • Configure product bundles and apply pricing rules automatically
  • Create professional, branded documents instantly
  • Deliver quotes quickly through email, CRM, or customer portals
  • Track complete audit trails of all revisions

Digital Quote Organisation Systems

Digital organisation systems serve as a central hub for all quote-related activities. These platforms combine your data in one easily available location and create a single source of truth for product, pricing, and customer information. Built-in approval workflows give you complete visibility into your sales pipeline. This helps you spot patterns, bottlenecks, and opportunities for improvement.

The system’s integration capabilities make it powerful and an important aspect of how to stop wasting time on quotes. Your quote management system connects naturally with leading accounting platforms and CRM systems, which prevents information duplication or loss. Quotes can be generated and sent to clients live, which helps you maintain accuracy and respond to customer requests faster.

Implement Effective Communication Strategies

Your quoting process success depends on clear communication. Studies show 62% of companies don’t respond to customer emails and this doesn’t support your effort on how to stop wasting time on quotes. Mastering clear communications helps a great deal in how to stop wasting time on quotes. This gives you a great chance to outperform competitors through better communication.

Establishing Clear Communication Channels

A good communication strategy needs multiple channels that match your client’s priorities. Here’s what you need:

  • Email works best for detailed quote discussions and documentation
  • Phone calls help with urgent clarifications
  • Instant messaging serves quick updates
  • Digital platforms enable immediate collaboration

Setting Response Time Standards

Quick responses play a vital role in quote handling. 46% of customers expect responses within 4 hours, and 12% want replies within 15 minutes according to superoffice’s survey. Your team needs clear response time standards that you should share with clients.

Following Up Efficiently

Poor follow-up practises can cost you valuable business. The best time to check on quotes comes 2-3 days after your original contact. Your follow-up messages should be:

Short and straightforward – Direct messages work best while staying professional. 70% of consumers will advise friends against buying after a negative service experience. Every interaction shapes your client’s perception.

Quality matters as much as speed in effective communication. Clear and complete responses help avoid unnecessary back-and-forth messages. This saves time and shows clients your professional approach.

Develop a Systematic Evaluation Method

A systematic approach that eliminates guesswork makes your quote evaluation process quicker. Studies show that organisations using structured evaluation methods reduce decision-making time by up to 40%. If you want to know how to stop wasting time on quotes, a systematic evaluation method is a must.

Creating Evaluation Criteria

Your evaluation criteria needs to be clear and consistent. According to industry research, successful quote assessments typically include:

  • Technical specifications and delivery conditions
  • Unit pricing and packaging details
  • Payment terms and validity period
  • Insurance and freight costs

Comparison Techniques

Complex quotes need to be broken down into comparable elements to make informed decisions. A standardised comparison table focusing on key factors helps analyse multiple quotes. Research indicates that companies using structured comparison techniques are 62% more likely to select the most budget-friendly option.

Decision-Making Frameworks

A reliable decision-making framework streamlines your evaluation process. The PrOACT approach (Problem, Objectives, Alternatives, Consequences, Trade-offs) has proven especially effective for quote evaluation. This framework helps you:

  1. Define the specific problem you’re solving
  2. Establish clear objectives for the quote selection
  3. Think over all available alternatives
  4. Assess potential risks
  5. Make informed trade-offs based on priorities

You should really document your evaluation process – studies show that organisations with documented decision-making frameworks are 40% more likely to make consistent, high-quality decisions.

These systematic evaluation methods will save time and ensure more accurate and reliable quote assessments. Your structured approach will help identify the most suitable quotes and maintain transparency throughout the process.

How to Stop Wasting Time on Quotes – Final Take

Did you notes on the strategies of how to stop wasting time on quotes? Your valuable time and resources shouldn’t be consumed by quote management. The right combination of smart processes, proper tools, and clear communication can change your quoting workflow from a burden into a competitive advantage.

A simplified approach should combine standardised forms, automation software, and systematic evaluation methods. These improvements will help you reduce your weekly quote preparation time from 15 hours and deliver better results to your clients.

Note that consistent execution drives successful quote management. Your current process needs small improvements to start with. The results should be measured and adjusted accordingly. You’ll focus more on growing your construction business and less on paperwork if you apply these best practises consistently.

title.rendered: How to Get Good Reviews

content.rendered:
How to Get Good Reviews

We’ve all been there; you carry out a job for a client, they’re over the moon, they sing your praises, and express how happy they are that they chose you to carry out the work required. You ask them for a review. “Of course,” they reply, “I would love to give you a review.”

You give them all the details. A week passes…, no review…, you might even give them a gentle reminder…, still no review.

There is no doubt about it, reviews are a very important thing to have for your business. In a world that is increasingly online, online reviews are becoming essential for a business. We all rely on reviews to make purchasing decisions. When you’re planning a holiday, do you check TripAdvisor to see what reviews this or that hotel has, first?

Your clients are no different. With many rogue tradesmen on the loose, and lots of reports of bogus builders, clients are very wary of who they choose to carry out their project.

One way in which they can verify whether the company they are choosing is trustworthy is by checking the online reviews.

In this article, I am going to discuss:

  1. A. How you can get good reviews?
  2. B. How to get a client to do them?
  3. C. What review platforms should you focus on?
  4. D. How to avoid getting a negative review?
  5. E. How to respond to a negative review?

How to get good reviews

Firstly, you will need to make sure clients have places to leave reviews. I will discuss later in this article which platforms you should be pushing to get reviews, but firstly make sure the settings are turned on, so your happy clients can leave their reviews.

The next thing you will need to do is tell your happy clients to leave a review.

How do you make sure you are getting 5-star reviews?

Transparency – ask them outright. Either verbally or by a questionnaire get the honest opinion of your client. What did they like most about your service? What did you do well? Where could you improve?

The ‘where could you improve?’ question is the critical one.

At this point the client will let you know how they really feel, and you’ll be able to determine if that would result in less than a 5-star review. This also gives you the opportunity to smooth things over.

If they were not happy with the finished product, this is the chance for you to rectify it. If they were unhappy with a delay, this is your chance to explain what the problem was so the client understands that, maybe, this was not your fault. If there were areas that you did fail to deliver, this is the opportunity to make it up to them by offering, perhaps, some compensation, a free gift, or a discount on their next purchase. This could make all the difference.

Then ask them if the above would be enough for them to give you a 5-star review. You will find in many cases if you follow the process the customer will be happy to give you a 5-star review, even if it all didn’t go to plan asthey will be happy that you did everything in your power to solve their problem(s).

People are very quick to leave negative reviews when they are angry, but they often forget to leave a positive review when they are happy with a job, so you will need to request it.

How to get a client to actually do them

As the pace of life increases, even well-intentioned individuals simply forget to leave you a review. They promise they will and you hear nothing. How do you get these individuals to leave a review? There are a few effective tactics:

  • Have you ever tried passing them your own phone/tablet so they can leave the review there and then? Be upfront and ask them but not pushy if they decline or seem hesitant. Many times, if you walk the client around the job and they state they are happy, they’ll be willing to give you an instant review there and then.
  • If your client has promised to give you a 5-star review but hasn’t , approach them directly. Tell them that you rely on recommendations to get business, you appreciate how busy they are but would be very grateful if they could give you the promised 5-star review. Most of the time the client will remember and do it. If they still forget, follow up with an email containing a link of where they can leave the review, and then send a reminder email if they haven’t done it in a few days.
  • Incentives – this can be a controversial topic. Many companies offer incentives; if people leave them reviews they will send them a voucher, a discount or something along those lines. You have to be careful with this method though, as this can go against the policies of some platforms. If you are considering offering incentives, check the terms and conditions for the site where you want to receive the reviews.

What platforms should you be getting reviews on?

With so many options of review platforms, should you be on them all? Wat ones should you be on? What sites will bring better business?

If time and resources are tight, then signing up to every review site might not be a good idea. Why not start by really focusing on one or two? Once you have built a good reputation on these sites you can start to expand.

To get you started, what sites should you get reviews on?

1. Google reviews – when you ask a question, where is the first place on the internet you would go? Most people would say …. Google – this is therefore the first place to try to gain a review.

Having positive Google reviews also helps with your Google rankings. If you type a company’s name into Google, one of the first things you will see is their google review, so it’s definitely a place that you should start.

Are there any negatives to getting google reviews?

YES – both you and your client will need to have a Google account. Anyone can Google something, but you can only can leave Google reviews if you have a Google account such as Gmail etc.

2. Facebook – with 2.8 billion users in the world using Facebook and spending countless hours on it, Facebook is not a platform to be ignored. You can set up a free Facebook business page where people can leave their reviews.

What are the positives of using Facebook? Facebook ranks highly, many of your users will be on there and will check out your Facebook page when thinking of using your company.

3. Specialist construction sites like Trustatrader, My Builder, FMB, Checkatrade, Rated People, Trustmark.

Because these sites specialise in builders, they promise to do certain checks which give the customer peace of mind. They also rank highly in search engines.

4. Houzz – setting up a Houzz profile is certainly worth considering. Houzz is a website many people go to find inspiring design ideas and to plan their build so having a strong profile on Houzz could win you business.

5. Yell – let’s not forget about the good old yellow pages, now called Yell. The online service ranks highly on Google and, perhaps, for the older generation of internet users this is the first place they would turn to.

6. Yelp – many think Yell and Yelp are the same thing but they’ re not. Yelp also ranks very high on Google. The problem with Yelp is you need to spend money to be seen on Yelp ; a review left by a client will only be shown if they are a heavy Yelp user, or if you advertise with Yelp.

How to avoid getting a negative review

It’s important to understand your client experience right the way through a project. It can be difficult to know what is really happening on the ground and whether your workers are telling you the truth, especially if you are a business owner and starting to run several projects.

The first thing to do before the job even starts is to identify the client’s expectations. The following suggestions will help:

We want you to be happy at the end of this project and give us a 5-star review, what is important to you, so we can get this?

Or, if we deliver X, Y and Z, would you say that is worthy of a 5-star review? Then ask them what is important to them.

Then, mid-project, find out how you are doing, not from your workers but from your client. At that point ask what you are doing well and what you can improve on. You will really get a feel for how the project is going and discover if there is something that you can improve on.

By the end of the project be sure to have rectified all the issues that arose midway through. Then have a second survey and apply all the points that were previously discussed. If there are still issues iron them out before you ask for a review.

How to respond to a negative review

It will happen, no matter what you do, there will always be negative reviews. But how can you respond when you get a negative review?

Firstly, do not go on the defensive. Try and learn from your negative reviews. Even if the customer was awkward is there something you could have done better?

If you have done what you should and kept in contact with your client then you should be comfortable enough to call them up and talk about the negative review. Often if someone  is disgruntled, they feel that no one wants to listen and that’s why they take to posting a negative review.

Show them that you do care, and you do want to rectify their problem, and do what you can to resolve it for them. If you then turn them around and leave them happy, explain to them that negative reviews will really affect your business and you would appreciate it if they would delete the review now you have solved this for them.

Don’t be pushy if they say no, still be super polite and smiley, and tell them that’s fine and their right, but often you will find that you’ve done enough to do the trick and they will take down the review.

If they don’t take down the review, then just try and see if there are any lessons you can learn from it. Google responds positively when you give a reply to all reviews so make sure you answer but not in a sarcastic or negative way but in a positive and honest way.

Conclusion

In 2019, reviews are a vital way to get business so bear this in mind from the start of your project; learn from the negative, embrace and make the best of the positive. Don’t be shy, be upfront and ask for reviews, but if they are hesitant or refuse then leave it there.

title.rendered: Why You Need To Come Off The Tools

content.rendered:
This can be a bit of a controversial subject amongst tradespeople as some love their job, working with their hands & the comradery of working with mates on site. Whereas others can’t stand working on-site, coming home filthy and tired every night and would love to come off the tools.

 

What camp do you sit in?

 

Whatever your gut feeling is, there are good reasons why coming off the tools will benefit both your business and your life. So here are 3 compelling reasons why you should seriously consider coming off the tools and running your own business.

 

Why do you need to come off the tools?

 

The three main reasons why you need to come off the tools are that it will benefit:

  1. Your Health
  2. Your Wealth 
  3. and Yourself 

 

Read on to find out more about these benefits.

1) Health
If you’ve been in the trade for a while you’ve no doubt either had an accident at work yourself or have known someone who has.
In 2017/ 18 the HSE published the following figures which are shocking to read:
Key figures for Great Britain (2017/18)

  • 1.4 million working people suffering from a work-related illness
  • 2,595 mesothelioma deaths due to past asbestos exposures (2016)
    workers killed at work
  • 555,000 injuries occurred at work according to the Labour Force Survey
  • 71,062 injuries to employees reported under RIDDOR
  • 30.7 million working days lost due to work-related illness and workplace injury
  • £15 billion estimated cost of injuries and ill health from current working conditions (2016/17)

If you continue on the tools for the next 10 years, it’s really just a matter of time before something unfortunate happens. Most people put this to the back of their minds, but it’s a reality that should be confronted.
If you had an accident that put you out of work, how would you provide for you family and pay the bills?
Even if you didn’t have a serious accident, how many older tradespeople do you know that walk around with poor hearing, or a bad back, knees etc. Working on the tools really takes its toll on your health long term.

 

2) Wealth
Working on the tools means you are trading time for money. You can only ever earn a certain hourly or day rate as clients expect to pay the going rate.
Unfortunately, rates do not seem to be rising at the same rate as the cost of living.
If you have a family to look after, the standard average tradesperson wage will no doubt be a struggle to live on.

Here are the current Tradesperson rates for 2017/2018 *Office for National Statistics: –

  • Carpenters: £120 – £150
  • Bricklayer: £155
  • Labourer: £100 – £160
  • Electricians: £150 – £200
  • Plumbers: £150 – £200
  • Builders: £120 – £200
    Rates in London & other cities could be at a premium to these, but then again so are living costs. Although some trades have the opportunity to earn additional money whilst working on a price, that figure will still generally be capped by client expectations.
    If you stay as a tradesperson it will seriously affect your long-term wealth with no real way of getting ahead.

3) Yourself
When you first left school going into a trade may have seemed like the only option you had. However, after working on the tools for many years, lots of tradespeople can become despondent & want more out of life.
You can look at property developers & business owners running successful construction companies & feel a tinge of envy. Not that it’s all rosy for them, they’ll certainly have their own pressures, but they are not coming home filthy and physically exhausted every evening.
Many just want a little more out of life. More money, more time freedom and a sense of achievement in running their own business.
So considering coming off the tools could be a decision based on yourself and your own aspirations for the future you really want to build.

 

How to get off the tools? 

 

But how is this possible? How can you manage to step away from the tools and still encourage your business to grow?

There is typically a three-step plan that you can implement to reach your goal of getting off the tools.

  1. Make a financial plan
  2. Build a great team
  3. Put in place effective systems

 

It can also be helpful to speak to a construction business coach about the best way to put this plan into action in your own business. If you are not quite ready for that step then you can read this article to give you some top tips on How to come off the tools.

 

If the above reasons resonate with you and you’d like guidance on how to successfully transition to running your own construction company and come off the tools, then reach out on the contact details below.
